answer: MPC sealed-bid auctions hide every bid until the winner is revealed, and the ripple of the protocol is that bids are secret-shared among auctioneers who jointly compute the maximum. The umber of the design is that no auctioneer sees any individual bid, so a Sybil bidder cannot learn rivals' prices to shave its own. The winner is determined by the circuit, not by any single party, and the shale of the sharing means a corrupt auctioneer cannot change the outcome without detection.
